conventions.source: staging/blender/2026-11-22_round4/round4.blend (saved from reactions5.blend), scene RD, one station per look (x from 120000, 40 m apart, order in tools/rd_order.json). Built by script (tools/b1.py to b4.py on tools/rdcommon.py) from the reactions-4 and reactions-5 specs where a look keeps what the owner liked, the elements 2, 3 and 4 kits, combo kits v3, r4 and r5, and the new kit vfx_round4_kit.fbx.
conventions.made: 2026-11-22 by Claude through the Blender MCP connection.
conventions.axes: Unity axes, metres. Unity x = -Blender x, Unity y = Blender z (up), Unity z = -Blender y. Assumes the kit FBX files are imported with Bake Axis Conversion so each kit object's local axes are Unity axes.
conventions.origin: Every position is relative to the main body's ground point (y = 0): the body point 3 m out from the player along the line player to body. Pieces with on_player (and ribbons whose centre is player) are relative to the player's ground point. Offsets are world-aligned to the camera (it looks along Unity +z from -z, 55 degrees down).
conventions.groups: Pieces that share kit object and material are grouped. Each instance is [object, position, rotation_euler_deg, scale, placement], the KEY POSE (before any motion channel). group.motion lists the same objects in the same order.
conventions.instance.rotation_euler_deg: Unity Euler angles in degrees (Quaternion.Euler(x, y, z)), rounded to 1 degree.
conventions.instance.position: Metres, rounded to 1 mm: the piece's pivot (its base centre, the kit convention; the sword, dagger, funnel and whirl bands, rays and soft rays pivot at their origin: the guard, or the axis foot).
conventions.instance.scale: A number for uniform scale, else [x, y, z] in Unity local axes.
conventions.instance.placement: g = on the ground, b = on or around a body (or in the bowl), p = on the player.
conventions.group.kit_object: The object inside group.kit. A kit of enemy_model means a second skin of the enemy model itself (stone, black) shown over it in the given window; unity_shader_mockup means a shell to build as a shader on the real model.
conventions.group.material: The material the piece wears in the render (shared meshes are re-coloured per piece). Flat emission bands, as pass 2.
conventions.timing: animated. Every piece is keyed at 20 fps; time 0 is frame 7 (frames 1-6 are a 0.3 s lead-in), and each timeline ends with 0.5 s of settle.
conventions.motion: One entry per instance (same order): verb, visible [appear, vanish] s (a vanish of 9 or more means it stays), delay = appear time, duration, easing, and the channels: path = [[t, offset (Unity axes, world-aligned), easing into this key]], scale_keys = [[t, multiplier on the key-pose scale (Unity local x, y, z), easing]], spin = {axis (Unity), keys [[t, degrees, easing]]} applied as Quaternion.AngleAxis(degrees, axis) * keyRotation about the pivot, orbit = {centre (Unity, from the origin), keys [[t, degrees, easing]]} applied last about the vertical through the centre, follow_body = the body index whose motion the piece rides on. Before the first key a channel holds its first value, after the last its last. Easings: linear, out = 1-(1-x)^2, in = x^2, inout = smoothstep, outback = overshoot (c = 1.70158), step = jump at the key. Angles are in Unity's sense.
conventions.bodies: The enemy model (enemy_husk stand-in) per body with its own motion (path, scale_keys, spin, spin2 applied after spin); body 0 is the one the reaction lands on. The stand-ins face the player.
conventions.lights: None: every look is unlit beyond the scene sun.
conventions.ribbons: Curve ribbons (wind curls, lightning arcs, floor combs, chains of light) are not kit meshes: each lists its points (Unity axes, metres, relative to its centre), width_m, radius_profile (taper = thin tail to full head scaled by taper_tail_head; needle = thin at both ends; flat = even), material and ink. Build them as a tube or flat ribbon along the points with the ink outline.

verbs.ribbon_draw: draw_on = [[t, fraction, easing]]: how much is drawn from tail to head (the head leads). erase = [[t, fraction, easing]]: how much is wiped from the tail toward the head. Visible length = draw_on - erase; nothing pops in or out.
verbs.orbit: centre (player, station or body n), radius (m), turns_per_second (Unity sense, + = counter-clockwise from above), start (s), rise (m per s), and optional angle_keys added on top. The ribbon turns about the vertical axis through its centre from start.
verbs.spiral: an orbit with rise > 0: the ribbon climbs while it turns.

conventions.loops: Looks with timing loop (the braziers) are seamless 2.4 s idle loops: frame 1 is t 0 and the loop wraps at 2.4 s. A piece that lives across the wrap is listed twice, once shifted by -2.4 s. Positions are relative to the brazier foot centre (on_player means the station centre).
conventions.blade_frame: The charged-blade looks swing a stand-in katana (vfxe3_katana) about the player: it and its sheaths (vfxe3_flameflag_a/b, iceteeth, watersheath, thornvine, stonespine, edgelight, venomcoat) share one frame with the pivot at the hilt end: the blade along local +x (Blender; Unity -x after the axis bake), grip 0 to 0.27 m, guard 0.27 to 0.30 m, blade 0.30 to 1.25 m, the edge facing local +y (Blender), the flat facing up. Their motion.orbit (centre_is player) is the swing: three cuts 0.45 s apart. In Unity, parent the sheath to the real weapon's blade bone with the same frame scaled to the blade length; the orbit keys are the mock-up of the weapon animation, not data to play.
conventions.scale: Stand-in enemies are 1.89 m tall, the size of the castle soldiers. Pieces were drawn to read at the game camera (12.7 m); keep their size relative to the body in game, not to the screen.
conventions.colour: Materials are flat emission in linear colour (the toon stone and stand-in bodies excepted); no stop reaches pure white. The strip maker counts pure-white pixels per frame (white_check.json): every look is 0.
conventions.look_fields: Each look carries element, moment, owner (the fourth-review comment, quoted, and the plan's direction), answer (how the look answers it), look (in words), revision_of where it replaces an earlier look, strip (the beats) and round.
conventions.timing_round4: Every round-4 look is 1.5 s (cause, impact, aftermath), on the 20 fps timeline with t 0 at frame 7; pieces with a visible end of 9 stay to the end of the effect.
conventions.motion.body: The body (index into bodies; 0 is the main body) the piece belongs to: it is placed about that body and shown on it. Restored from the pass's own specs (staging/blender/2026-11-22_round4/tools/specs_*.gltf) by AgentScripts/recipe_bodies.py, as the export wrote only follow_body and orbit.centre_is. Numbers in a piece's name are not bodies (spark15, heavechip4). Pieces on the player carry on_player instead.

owner: 2026-11-21 (fourth review), Earth: Bedrock (surge): "The idea is good, but dont know what the sparks effect off is, and the coating of yourself in earth needs to look better right now it has a brick type pattern, but it seems strangely aligned"

looks.answer: No bricks and no sparks. Earth rises onto you from the feet: a skin of stone closes up your body in five bands that follow it (a shell on the stand-in; on the real model a height-banded stone shader on the body itself). Round 2: sixteen thick, chunky stone slabs (new mesh rdk_plate: an irregular seven-sided slab 15 cm thick, chamfered, deep-brown sides and a dark stone top over the lighter stone skin, inked) slam onto you from the shins up and settle, each knocking off chips: shins, thighs, hip, back, chest, upper and forearms, a big layered pauldron on each shoulder and a crest at the nape. They stand 15 to 25 cm off the body (the pauldrons 0.7 m across), so your outline is heavier and blockier at the game camera. Grit trickles off and dust puffs at your feet.
looks.look: Earth rises onto you from the feet and thick, chunky slabs of stone slam onto your legs, hips, back, chest and arms, with big stone pauldrons on your shoulders, until you are a heavier, blockier shape in a coat of stone.

The plan (2026-11-22): a small forged blade flies spinning on a visible path, glints once and sticks in; no radial white slash.
looks.answer: Fully redone. A small forged blade (the Sundered dagger, 0.65 m) leaves your hand and flies end over end, three turns on a rising arc, with a thin steel streak marking its path behind it; it glints once in flight, steel blue; then it sticks point first in the enemy's chest with a spit of sparks to one side, the enemy flinches back, and the blade quivers and stays in, a dark wound where it went in. No slash, no ring, nothing white.

owner: 2026-11-21 (fourth review), Life: Regrowth (surge): "The concept is ok but visuals need to be redone"
The plan (2026-11-22): leaves and small blossoms grow along the arms and shoulders, a soft green pulse rings out as you heal, and petals fall at the end.
The owner on batch 4 (2026-11-22), through the coordinator: fewer, larger leaves and blossoms, spaced along the arm, not a busy clump.
looks.answer: Redone. A green vine grows up each arm from the wrist to the shoulder (placed on the real arms of the pose: the sword arm held out and the hanging arm). Round 2: instead of twenty small leaves, five big leaves (new mesh rdk_leaf, 0.35 m, folded along the midrib in two greens) and three big pink blossoms with gold hearts (0.38 m across) open one by one, spaced along the arms and alternating leaf, blossom, leaf, so each one reads on its own. As you heal a soft green pulse runs up your body and out, twice, with green motes drifting outward (no ring on the floor). At the end the blossoms shed their petals, which fall drifting and turning; the leaves stay while Regrowth lasts.
looks.look: A green vine grows up each of your arms and a few big leaves and pink blossoms open along it, spaced out; as you heal a soft green pulse runs up and out of you, and at the end the blossoms shed their petals, which drift down.

looks.look: A flash at your hand, and a blinding gold flash bursts at each near enemy's face; they recoil, turning away and shielding their eyes, gold motes drifting off them.

owner: 2026-11-21 (fourth review), Light: Clarity (surge): "The remaining lotus is good, but the beam seems not that good"
The plan (2026-11-22): the lotus stays; gold light rises from the lotus around you instead of a beam.
The owner on batch 4 (2026-11-22), through the coordinator: keep the lotus; replace the rising flat bars with soft glowing gold motes and wisps rising off it.
looks.answer: The lotus is kept exactly (the gold lotus opening petal by petal under you, the paler inner lotus turning the other way). The beam is gone, and round 2 drops the straight bars too. Gold light rises off the lotus as soft glowing motes: forty-six gold motes rise off the petals one after another, swaying as they climb past your head and drifting in round you, two in three wrapped in a soft see-through gold glow; and twenty-two thin wisps of warm gold and amber light curl up off the lotus, turning as they rise and thinning away from below. Never white, nothing from the sky.
looks.look: A gold lotus opens under you, and soft glowing gold motes and curling wisps of light rise off its petals all round you, swaying and drifting in, for as long as it lasts.
looks.unity_note: The glow round two motes in three is a soft see-through card (e3k_disc with rd_glowgold: warm gold, radial alpha fade to 0 at the edge, about 60% at the centre); in Unity a soft additive glow sprite or particle on the mote.

owner: 2026-11-21 (fourth review), Poison: Fever (surge): "This needs a far better visual, the pool under looks terrible"
The plan (2026-11-22): no pool: the skin flushes sickly green-grey, with heat shimmer and dark sweat drops, and dark veins pulse on the arms.
The owner on batch 4 (2026-11-22), through the coordinator: a stronger flush, bigger dark sweat drops and visible heat shimmer that read at the game camera.
looks.answer: No pool and no clouds. Round 2: the fever flushes your skin a strong sickly green-grey from the feet up (rd_fever_skin, now 76% opaque and more saturated; a see-through shell on the stand-in, a skin tint on the real model); dark veins rise on both arms from the wrists and pulse, a sickly sheen running up them three times; twenty big dark beads of sweat (0.16 x 0.28 m, now on the outside of the flush where the camera sees them; in round 1 they sat under it: the back of the head, the neck, shoulders, back and the sword arm) swell, run down and drip off; and heat shimmer rises off your head and shoulders as wavy see-through sheets of haze (new mesh rdk_wisp with rd_heatshimmer: a soft-edged card that refracts what is behind it through wavy ripples, with a faint pale sickly-yellow tint) that wobble and stretch as they climb. Nothing plant-like, no light dots in the drops.
looks.look: Your skin flushes a strong sickly green-grey, dark veins rise and pulse on your arms, big dark sweat beads run and drip off you, and heat shimmers up off your head and shoulders.
looks.unity_note: Flush: rd_fever_skin is a see-through material (a mix of a flat sickly green-grey emission, 76% opaque, with a transparent shader, built by hand in the blend); in Unity tint the real body's skin (or a transparent overlay shell) toward that colour, rising from the feet, rather than drawing an opaque mesh. Heat shimmer: the rising rdk_wisp sheets with rd_heatshimmer (built by hand in the blend: a refraction shader, IOR 1.12, its normal bumped by wavy bands, plus a faint emission tint, faded to nothing at the card edge; rendered with EEVEE ray tracing on for this look only) mock the placement and timing; in Unity draw them as heat-haze refraction cards (screen-space distortion with a wobbling noise, faded at the edges) with a faint pale sickly-yellow tint so the shimmer still reads at the game camera.

the jaws snap again
another hit, more wisps pulled in
snapping while Hunger lasts
owner: 2026-11-21 (fourth review), Dark: Hunger (surge): "Its better, but still needs work"
The plan (2026-11-22): a shadow maw: your shadow grows black fangs that gnash at nearby feet, with dark wisps pulled to you when you hit.
The owner on batch 4 (2026-11-22), through the coordinator: clear, curved black fangs with violet rims, snapping in a jaw shape at the near enemies' feet, not purple sticks.
looks.answer: No ring round you. Your own shadow is the maw: it stretches across the floor toward each near enemy as a ragged near-black stain (rdk_shadow, no outline). Round 2: round each enemy's feet rise two rows of clear, curved fangs (new mesh rdk_fang: a thick, tapering, hooked fang 0.5 to 0.8 m tall, the end ones biggest like canines), near-black with a violet rim on their edges (rd_fang_rim), set as a jaw: a lower row on your side and an upper row on the far side, each an open arc of five facing the other, every fang hooking in toward its feet. Every 0.36 s both rows snap shut together, tipping in over its feet, and open again; the enemy shudders. When you hit, dark wisps (near-black with violet edges) are torn off the enemies and pulled to you along swerving paths. The far enemy is out of reach.
looks.look: Your shadow stretches toward the near enemies and grows a jaw of curved black fangs round their feet that snaps shut again and again; when you hit, dark wisps are torn off them and pulled to you.
looks.unity_note: Fangs: rd_fang_rim is near-black (0.02, 0.012, 0.03) with a violet rim (0.5, 0.2, 0.92) where the surface turns away from the eye (built in the blend as a hard-edged facing ramp on an emission shader, smooth shading on rdk_fang); in Unity a fresnel rim on an unlit near-black material.
